name: Anantara Stanley and Livingstone Victoria Falls Hotel
insider_take: This legendary hotel sits just 500 meters from one of the world's seven natural wonders, where the thunderous roar of Victoria Falls creates a constant symphony of nature's power.
whats_special: Built in 1904, this historic property is named after explorer Dr. David Livingstone and journalist Henry Morton Stanley. The hotel's prime location offers unobstructed views of the Zambezi River and the spray from "Mosi-oa-Tunya" (The Smoke That Thunders). During full moon nights, guests can witness the rare lunar rainbow phenomenon over the falls - a magical spectacle visible only from this privileged vantage point.
pro_tip: Book a room on the falls-facing side during dry season (September-December) for the clearest views, or visit during peak flow (March-May) to experience the falls' full thundering power and dramatic mist clouds.
dont_miss: Take the hotel's private walking path directly to the falls viewpoints, enjoy high tea on the terrace while elephants drink from the Zambezi below, and experience the sunset cruise where hippos and crocodiles share the waters just meters from your boat. The hotel's century-old heritage railway station connects directly to the famous Victoria Falls Bridge.
pros: Prime location with direct views of Victoria Falls
Historic colonial charm combined with modern luxury amenities
Multiple dining venues offering international and local cuisine
cons: Remote destination requiring planned travel arrangements
